## Claims
- [source-backed] The paper’s formal conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are inclusion-minimal; “minimal” means no proper subset generates. [source-6, lines 14-16; source-6, lines 41-44]
- [source-backed] The authors report only finite computational verification, for bigrassmannians with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6, lines 46-54]
- [source-backed] The stronger suspected statement is \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), and the source says a proof had eluded the authors. [source-6, lines 56-72]
- [proved] A universal common-cardinality assertion over \(\mathbb Z\) is false. Let \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\) and \(I=(2x,3x)=(x)\). Both \(\{x\}\) and \(\{2x,3x\}\) are homogeneous generating sets; the latter is inclusion-minimal since \(x\notin(2x)\) and \(x\notin(3x)\). Their cardinalities are \(1\) and \(2\).
- [proved] Let \(R=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}R_d\) with \(R_0=\mathbb Z\), \(R_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}R_d\), and let \(M\) be a bounded-below, finitely generated graded \(R\)-module. Put \(Q=M/R_+M\). Homogeneous generating sets of \(M\) are inclusion-minimal exactly when their images are inclusion-minimal homogeneous \(\mathbb Z\)-generating sets of \(Q\): if the images generate \(Q\), then \(M=N+R_+M\), where \(N\) is generated by the lifts; the bounded-below graded Nakayama argument gives \(M=N\).
- [proved] Under these hypotheses, all inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets of \(M\) have a common cardinality if and only if every nonzero graded abelian group \(Q_d\) is finite \(p_d\)-primary for some prime \(p_d\) (the prime may depend on \(d\)). In that case the common cardinality is \(\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb F_{p_d}}(Q_d/p_dQ_d)\). Sufficiency follows from Nakayama over the local ring \(\mathbb Z/p_d^{e_d}\). Conversely, a free summand yields the irredundant alternatives \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) in \(\mathbb Z\); two distinct primary parts yield respectively an irredundant union of primary generators and an irredundant CRT-aligned generating set, of different sizes.
- [proved] Consequently, freeness of \(M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(\mathbb Z\), even if established, does not by itself imply common cardinality for arbitrary inclusion-minimal generating sets: \(\mathbb Z\) is free but has the irredundant generating sets \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\).

## Strategy
Reduce homogeneous generation modulo positive degree, then apply the classification of finitely generated abelian groups with invariant irredundant-generator cardinality.

## Gaps
The supplied excerpts do not contain the exact text of “accepted claim 9” or the formal source lines 1489–1552. Thus this refutes the general \(\mathbb Z\)-assertion, but does not decide whether extra special structure of the particular ideals \(J_v\) enforces minimality.

## Next
Obtain the exact claim-9 formulation and identify its quotient \(M/R_+M\); test whether each graded quotient is finite primary, or whether a stronger argument specific to the proposed Schur generators is required. Independent review remains absent.
